architecture.mechanism: Supercritical CO2 stores thermal energy in compressed dense-phase fluid within field-proven geological traps, leveraging pressure headroom and caprock sealing to maintain stable conditions over long durations without active energy input.
architecture.intervention: Replace phase-change gel packs with a small pressurized vessel of supercritical CO2 (or a CO2/H2O mixture engineered for the 2–8 °C range using throttling/Joule-Thomson expansion) integrated into the shipping container as the latent/sensible cold reservoir, exploiting the high volumetric energy density of dense-phase CO2 to cut weight while using a passive pressure-relief orifice to draw cooling on demand.
architecture.expected_effect: Maintains the 96-well microplate at 2–8 °C for ≥72 hours in hot ambient conditions with substantially lower parcel mass than gel-pack systems and no battery, electronics, or ice resupply.
architecture.falsification_test: Ship three replicate parcels (each holding a 96-well plate instrumented with calibrated temperature loggers and a supercritical-CO2 cold capsule) for 72 hours in a controlled chamber at 35 °C/70% RH; the 2–8 °C window is met if ≥2/3 plates stay continuously within range; compare mean parcel mass against an identical shipment using gel packs and require ≥30% mass reduction.
